title: one shared intrinsic basis, many Mirror task coordinates
hypothesis: A shared random intrinsic basis plus one Mirror angle per task gives a useful byte/quality frontier across 256 aligned tasks versus independent SAID codes and direct two-coefficient codes; unrelated task codes need richer state.
physical_object: shared 32D linear predictor and an 8D random orthonormal task-update basis
mirror_coordinate: one FP16 angle/task on a fixed-radius circle in two paid basis columns
logical_multiplicity: 256 task-conditioned functions; task count is not interpreted as independent capacity
controls: PA33 SAID-8 with per-task FP32 intrinsic vectors

data.unrelated_teacher: theta_t = theta0 + P @ z_t, z_t iid Gaussian in R^8

selection.tunable: none; all dimensions, code precision and 720-point angle grid are frozen

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes after reload

success_gate: All development seeds: Mirror normalized test MSE <=1e-4, total actual bytes <=90% direct 2-coefficient control and <=75% SAID-8, and within 1e-5 absolute normalized MSE of the direct control.
failure_gate: Any aligned nearest-control quality/byte gate fails, or unrelated codes require richer state without an aligned actual-byte frontier point.

fresh.open_condition: only if every development world passes all aligned quality and actual-byte gates

boundaries: teacher uses the Mirror circular chart
task IDs supplied; no learned router
